correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the real-projective proof. On each of at most four arcs cut by the axes and nonzero row kernels, the difference of p-th norm powers is a signed homogeneous binary form of degree p. If it vanishes identically and all entries are nonzero, the two mixed coefficients imply equality of the row ratios because p−2 is odd; proportionality then makes the signed terms cancel, inconsistent with the positive pure powers on the right. With a zero entry the same equations force both rows to be coordinate-supported; the pure terms then force different coordinates and equal magnitudes, the excluded scaled signed permutation. This handles zero rows and coincident marks. A nonzero form has at most floor(p/2) distinct double roots on any arc closure: take an affine projective chart containing the closure and use differentiability of the original difference at every maximizing direction, including marked endpoints, to get the double-root condition. Four such counts, possibly overcounting endpoints, followed by antipodal lifting give 4(p−1). The cubic sentence is read as a specialization under the explicit standing exclusion of all scalar multiples of isometries, not a separate claim about every map that is not itself an isometry. Symbolic check only; no independent formal certificate or numerical exhaustion claimed.

evidence: Sain treats all integer p≥2 with 2(8p−5) points and discusses the Hilbert-space special case separately.
The even-p record proves at most p points for even p, with an example sharp at p=4. The skew involution record counts exactly four points for one operator family at sufficiently large real p.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader exponent range of the first theorem carries a weaker bound. The sharper even-p result does not apply at odd p, and the large-p operator family is not a uniform result over real matrices.

evidence: For odd p≥3, 4p−4 < 16p−10. A single binary-form polynomial across the projective line at even p does not supply a polynomial of the same type at odd p; separate sign-polynomial arcs are needed.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither substituting odd p into the known integer theorem nor applying the sharper result for even p implies this point bound. The nonvanishing sector argument and multiple-root count do the additional work.

value.rationale: This addresses the optimum-cardinality problem posed in the prior literature by materially tightening the available uniform bound (for example 38 to 8 at p=3), with a short argument that handles all matrices under the precise exclusion, rather than one special example. The significance is the uniform upper bound, not resolution of the exact maximum.
